title: Cancer Health Drivers Training Program
summary: The Cancer Health Drivers Training Program at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill offers postdoctoral training on cross-cutting health disparity issues across the cancer continuum, from etiology and primary prevention to survivorship. The program includes the major cancers and addresses risk factors, epidemiological bases of disparities, detection, epidemiology, research methods, prevention and control, promotion, screening, communication, community-based participatory research and policy. Fellows receive up to two years of funding. At the end of each year, each fellow’s performance is evaluated and funding for the next year depends on the progress made. Fellows are assigned faculty mentors in more than one discipline and benefit from the UNC’s highly collaborative, productive and multidisciplinary faculty. title: Mobilizing Research Fellowship 2026: 23 Fellowships of $12,500 for International Graduate Students at Memorial University
summary: International graduate students with research projects in science and technology now have an opportunity to develop their research beyond the laboratory and explore its potential for commercialization. The Mobilizing Research Fellowship Program 2026 at Memorial University of Newfoundland and Labrador is offering 23 fellowships valued at $12,500 each to eligible international graduate students. The program is designed to help researchers bridge the gap between academic research and real-world application by developing skills in technology innovation, entrepreneurship, intellectual property, translational research and commercialization. Applications are currently being accepted, and interested students must submit their applications by Monday, August 24, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Mobilizing Research Fellowship 2026 at Memorial University The Mobilizing Research Fellowship Program is a specialized initiative designed for international graduate students undertaking research-based programs at Memorial University . Rather than focusing solely on academic research, the program encourages participants to consider how scientific and engineering discoveries can be transformed into practical solutions, products, technologies or services that respond to real-world and market needs. The fellowship therefore provides an opportunity for graduate researchers to develop skills that extend beyond traditional academic training. Participants will learn how to think about their research from an innovation and entrepreneurial perspective while receiving guidance from mentors and participating in workshops and coursework. The program will support 23 fellows , with each fellowship valued at $12,500 . The overall program runs from September 10, 2026, through April 30, 2027 , and participation in the scheduled activities is mandatory. What Is the Mobilizing Research Fellowship Program? The Mobilizing Research Fellowship Program is intended to help graduate researchers translate research discoveries into commercially viable outcomes. Many research projects begin with scientific questions or technical challenges in laboratories and universities. However, moving an idea from research to a practical product, service or technology can require a different set of skills, including entrepreneurship, intellectual property management, market analysis, professional communication and innovation strategy. This fellowship addresses that gap by giving selected graduate students structured exposure to these areas. The program uses a From Lab Bench to Store Shelves approach to translational research and development. Through workshops, coursework, coaching and practical activities, participants will be encouraged to think about how their research could respond to market needs and potentially create real-world impact. The program can be particularly valuable for students who see a future for themselves not only in academic research but also in industry, government, entrepreneurship or technology commercialization. Objectives of the Mobilizing Research Fellowship The fellowship is designed around several key objectives. 1. Develop interdisciplinary innovation skills Participants will gain exposure to disciplines and skills that complement their academic research. These include technology innovation, entrepreneurship and the process of translating research discoveries into practical applications. This interdisciplinary approach can help students understand how scientific knowledge interacts with business, industry and society. 2. Build an entrepreneurial mindset The program encourages students to look at their research from an entrepreneurial perspective. Rather than asking only whether a research question is scientifically interesting, participants will also be encouraged to consider questions such as: What problem does the research address? Who could benefit from the resulting technology or discovery? Could the research lead to a product or service? What market need could the research potentially address? What barriers could prevent the research from reaching users? How could intellectual property be managed? What would be required to move the research toward commercialization? This mindset can be useful for researchers interested in entrepreneurship, technology transfer and innovation. 3. Strengthen professional competencies The fellowship also aims to prepare participants for professional environments outside traditional academic research. Students will have opportunities to develop competencies that may be useful when working with companies, investors, government organizations, research institutions and entrepreneurial teams. 4. Prepare researchers for diverse career paths The program is intended to prepare participants for careers in: Academia Industry Government Research and development Technology commercialization Entrepreneurship Scientist- or engineer-led ventures This makes the fellowship particularly relevant to graduate students who want to understand how research can be translated into broader professional and economic impact. What Does the Fellowship Offer? Selected participants will receive access to a combination of financial support, training, mentorship and practical experience. Fellowship funding The program offers 23 fellowships of $12,500 . The fellowships are intended to support participants while they undertake the required program activities and develop their research mobilization and commercialization skills. The fellowships are contingent upon final funding approval from the Department of Jobs, Growth and Rural Development, Office of Immigration and Multiculturalism, Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, Newfoundland and Labrador Settlement and Integration Program (NLSIP) . Training and Learning Opportunities Fellows will participate in a range of activities designed to complement their existing research expertise. Translational R D workshops Participants will receive training in translational research and development using the From Lab Bench to Store Shelves model and methodology. This component focuses on understanding how research discoveries can potentially move from academic environments toward practical applications and market opportunities. Entrepreneurship and innovation course Participants will take a graduate course focused on new venture creation , entrepreneurship, innovation and professional skills. The course is scheduled for Thursdays from 5:00 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. in BN-1009 . Students who apply should therefore ensure that they can attend the course throughout the program. One-on-one mentorship Fellows will receive individual coaching from mentors within the entrepreneurial ecosystem. This can give participants an opportunity to receive guidance on their ideas, research applications, commercialization potential and professional development. Real-world experience The program also includes practical workshops designed to help researchers align their projects with actual market needs. This practical component is important because successful commercialization often requires researchers to understand not only the technical strength of an innovation but also the problem it solves and the people or organizations that may ultimately use it. Who Is Eligible for the Mobilizing Research Fellowship? The program is specifically designed for international graduate students enrolled in research-based programs at Memorial University . Applicants must meet several eligibility conditions. Applicants must be international graduate students The fellowship is open to international graduate students who are currently enrolled in a research-based program at Memorial University . Importantly, Postdoctoral Fellows are not eligible to apply. Research must be related to science and technology Applicants must bring a project that aligns with science and technology disciplines . The proposed research should also have potential for commercialization. This means applicants should be able to demonstrate that their research could potentially lead to a practical application, technology, product, service or other commercially relevant outcome. Applicants must remain students throughout the program Applicants must be students for the entire program period, which runs from: September 10, 2026, to April 30, 2027. Students who expect to graduate or otherwise cease to be students before the end of the program should carefully consider this requirement before applying. Valid study permit required Applicants must have a valid study permit for the duration of the program . This is an important eligibility requirement for international students and should be confirmed before submitting an application. Location and Attendance Requirements The program has significant in-person participation requirements. Normally, participants must be present in St. John s for the duration of the program . There are limited exceptions for: Participants conducting field studies Participants located in person on the Grenfell campus Participants located in person on the Labrador campus Applicants should therefore be prepared for substantial in-person participation rather than treating the fellowship as a fully remote program. Mandatory Program Commitment Applicants should carefully consider the time commitment before applying. All program activities are mandatory. In addition to completing the new venture creation graduate course, participants must be able to dedicate at least five hours per week to other program activities. These activities can include workshops and sessions covering areas such as: Translational research and development Intellectual property management Professionalism Entrepreneurship Innovation Entrepreneurial thinking and mindset Most of these additional activities are expected to take place on Fridays from 1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. The combination of coursework and additional activities means applicants should make sure their academic and research schedules can accommodate the fellowship requirements. Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable for Graduate Researchers Graduate students often develop highly specialized scientific or technical expertise during their research. However, technical knowledge alone may not be enough to move a discovery into practical use. The Mobilizing Research Fellowship addresses this challenge by giving students opportunities to develop complementary skills. Participants can learn how to: Identify potential applications for research discoveries. Consider market needs alongside scientific objectives. Understand the fundamentals of entrepreneurship. Explore intellectual property considerations. Communicate research ideas in professional and commercial contexts. Think about technology transfer and commercialization. Work with mentors and members of the entrepreneurial ecosystem. Develop professional skills that can be applied beyond academia. These experiences could be especially useful for students considering careers where science, engineering, innovation and business intersect. From Research to Commercialization One of the most important aspects of the fellowship is its emphasis on moving research toward commercialization. Academic research can produce discoveries with significant potential, but transforming a discovery into something that can be used in the marketplace can involve numerous stages. These can include: Identifying a real-world problem Validating whether a solution addresses that problem Understanding potential users or customers Assessing market needs Considering intellectual property Developing an innovation strategy Exploring business or venture opportunities Building professional networks Understanding commercialization pathways The fellowship introduces participants to these concepts so that they can begin thinking about the broader potential of their research. Who Should Consider Applying? This opportunity may be particularly suitable for international graduate students whose research has a strong connection to science, technology, engineering or innovation and who are interested in exploring the commercial or entrepreneurial potential of their work. Potential applicants may include researchers who are interested in: Technology commercialization Research and development Entrepreneurship Scientific innovation Engineering innovation Startups and new ventures Intellectual property Industry collaboration Technology transfer Translational research Academic entrepreneurship Applicants should, however, carefully review the official eligibility requirements before applying because enrollment status, research area, immigration status and attendance requirements are important conditions of the program. Program Timeline Applicants should be aware of the following important dates and commitments: Date Program milestone August 24, 2026, 11:59 p.m. Application deadline September 10, 2026 Program begins September 10, 2026 – April 30, 2027 Fellowship/program participation period April 30, 2027 Program period ends Applicants should submit their materials before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours, particularly because the program has multiple eligibility and participation requirements. How to Apply for the Mobilizing Research Fellowship Interested applicants should complete the official 2026 Research Mobilization Fellowship Application Form . Before applying, prospective candidates should ensure that they: Are an international graduate student at Memorial University. Are enrolled in a research-based program. Are not a Postdoctoral Fellow. Have a science- or technology-related research project. Can demonstrate commercialization potential. Have a valid study permit for the entire program. Can remain a student throughout the program. Can commit to all mandatory activities. Can meet the course and weekly program requirements. Can satisfy the applicable in-person attendance requirements. To apply click HERE click HERE to learn more about this opportunity Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the Mobilizing Research Fellowship Program 2026 is: Monday, August 24, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Applicants should make sure their applications are completed and submitted before this deadline. Important Funding Note The fellowship funding is contingent upon final funding approval from the relevant Newfoundland and Labrador government departments and settlement and integration program. Applicants should therefore take this funding condition into consideration when reviewing the opportunity. Important Things Applicants Should Know Although the fellowship offers substantial benefits, applicants should understand that it requires a significant commitment. Before applying, consider the following: The fellowship is intended for international graduate students at Memorial University. Postdoctoral Fellows cannot apply. The research must be aligned with science and technology. The project must have commercialization potential. Participation in program activities is mandatory. Students must remain enrolled throughout the entire program. A valid study permit is required. The new venture creation course requires weekly attendance on Thursdays. Additional program activities require at least five hours per week. Most additional activities take place on Fridays. Participants are normally expected to be physically present in St. John s. Exceptions are limited to specific field-study or campus circumstances. The fellowship funding remains subject to final funding approval. Conclusion The Mobilizing Research Fellowship Program 2026 offers international graduate students at Memorial University an opportunity to take their scientific or technological research beyond traditional academic settings and explore its potential for commercialization. With 23 fellowships valued at $12,500 each , the program combines financial support with entrepreneurship education, translational R D workshops, mentorship, professional development and practical exposure to the innovation ecosystem. For graduate researchers interested in transforming scientific discoveries into practical solutions, launching ventures, working with industry or developing careers at the intersection of research and entrepreneurship, the program could provide valuable experience and professional connections. Eligible international graduate students should carefully review the requirements and prepare their applications ahead of the August 24, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. deadline . title: Free UN SDG Evaluation for Sustainable Development Pathway 2026: Study with UNIDO, the World Bank Group and UNDP
summary: The UN SDG Evaluation for Sustainable Development Learning Pathway brings together three complementary learning resources from the United Nations Industrial Development Organization, the World Bank Group and the United Nations Development Programme. The pathway begins with the foundations of evaluation, advances to rigorous impact-evaluation methods and concludes with a systems-thinking perspective for assessing complex and long-term change. It is important to describe the pathway accurately: it contains two formal self-paced online courses and one UNDP microlearning blog resource . The third component is not a conventional course and does not award a certificate, but it forms an official part of the pathway and adds an important practical perspective on evaluating systems change. About the UN SDG Evaluation for Sustainable Development Pathway UN SDG presents the pathway as a structured learning journey for developing essential knowledge and skills in evaluation for sustainable development. It introduces the principles, methodologies and tools used to assess the effectiveness and impact of policies and programmes. Its sequence is designed to take learners from core evaluation concepts to quantitative impact evaluation and then to the challenge of assessing change in interconnected systems. The pathway is associated with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and with SDG 17, particularly capacity-building, partnerships and systemic issues. Rather than treating evaluation as a narrow compliance exercise, the pathway shows how it can support institutional learning, evidence-based decision-making, policy improvement and accountability. Pathway at a glance Detail Information Pathway name Evaluation for Sustainable Development Platform UN SDG Learning providers UNIDO, World Bank Group and UNDP Components Two self-paced courses and one microlearning blog Delivery Fully online Language English Level Introductory, progressing from foundations to technical and systems-oriented material Cost The learning resources are free to access; the World Bank course can be audited free, while an optional verified edX certificate may require a fee Certificate No certificate for the UNIDO course; a certificate option is listed for the World Bank course; no certificate for the UNDP blog Deadline No fixed application or enrolment deadline is currently stated Official pathway Evaluation for Sustainable Development on UN SDG Why this learning pathway is valuable Monitoring can show whether activities took place, outputs were delivered or targets were reached. Evaluation goes further by examining the merit, relevance, effectiveness and consequences of an intervention. Impact evaluation adds another layer by asking whether observed outcomes were actually caused by the policy or programme. Systems-change evaluation then addresses an even harder question: how should progress be assessed when outcomes emerge through many interacting actors, institutions, incentives and external conditions? The pathway addresses these three levels in a logical order: Evaluation foundations: Understand what evaluation is, how it differs from related management functions and how an evaluation is planned and managed. Impact evaluation methods: Learn how experimental and statistical tools can help establish causal effects. Systems-change evaluation: Examine how to assess complex, long-term transformation when simple indicators and conventional attribution are insufficient. By combining institutional evaluation practice, quantitative impact methods and systems thinking, the pathway gives learners a broader understanding than any one component could provide independently. Resource 1: UNIDO Evaluation Training e-Learning The first component is the Evaluation Training e-Learning offered by the United Nations Industrial Development Organization. UN SDG classifies it as an introductory, self-paced online course. It is delivered in English, takes approximately three hours and is free. The official listing states that it does not provide a certificate. UNIDO developed the training through its Independent Evaluation Unit to strengthen understanding of evaluation principles and evaluation management. The course combines readings with interactive exercises intended to encourage participants to apply concepts to work-related situations. Main purpose of the UNIDO course The training is designed to give participants the information and practical understanding needed to take part in an evaluation or help manage one. It introduces the role of evaluation within UNIDO and the wider United Nations system while also addressing methods, evidence, stakeholder responsibilities and the management of an evaluation process. Structure of the UNIDO evaluation training The training consists of three modules: Module 1: Introduction to Evaluation in UNIDO The first module establishes a foundation in evaluation principles. It helps learners understand the different types of evaluation conducted within UNIDO, distinguish evaluation from other management functions such as monitoring and recognize the components of a credible evaluation in line with international norms. This distinction is particularly important in results-based management. Monitoring normally provides continuing information about implementation and performance, whereas evaluation applies criteria and evidence to reach a reasoned judgment about an intervention s design, implementation, results or value. Module 2: Evaluation Fundamentals and Approaches The second module introduces core evaluation concepts and approaches. It covers the six principal evaluation criteria referenced in UNIDO s training, UNIDO s approach to independent evaluation, evaluation methods, data analysis and other approaches used to examine programmes and projects. This module helps learners connect evaluation questions with suitable evidence and analytical methods. It also introduces the idea that evaluation design should be driven by the purpose of the assessment and the decisions that its findings are expected to support. Module 3: Commissioning and Managing Evaluations in UNIDO The final module focuses on the full process of planning, commissioning and managing an evaluation. It covers the five evaluation phases and their key principles, the tasks involved at different stages, the responsibilities of relevant stakeholders, common managerial challenges and practical and technical requirements. For professionals who may commission an external evaluation, coordinate consultants, review deliverables or support management responses, this component is especially useful. A technically sound evaluation can still fail if its scope is unclear, stakeholders are poorly coordinated, evidence requirements are unrealistic or findings are not linked to decisions. What learners can gain from the UNIDO course After completing the modules, learners should be better able to: Explain the purpose and role of evaluation within an organization; Distinguish evaluation from monitoring and other management functions; Recognize different types of evaluation; Understand the characteristics of a credible and useful evaluation; Identify key evaluation criteria, methods and analytical considerations; Understand the stages involved in commissioning and managing an evaluation; Recognize the responsibilities of commissioners, evaluators and other stakeholders; and Anticipate practical and managerial challenges during an evaluation. The course is available through the UNIDO Evaluation Training page , while its consolidated details are available on the UN SDG course listing . Resource 2: World Bank Group Evaluating Impact in Low- and Middle-Income Countries The second component is Evaluating Impact in Low- and Middle-Income Countries , a self-paced introductory course offered by the World Bank Group through edX. It was developed collaboratively by Georgetown University and the World Bank s Strategic Impact Evaluation Fund, with support from Georgetown and World Bank learning and research initiatives. According to UN SDG, the course has an estimated length of 24 weeks and requires approximately three to five hours of study per week. This represents an estimated total commitment of about 72 to 120 hours, depending on the learner s pace and the depth with which exercises and supporting materials are completed. What the World Bank impact-evaluation course covers Development programmes often report that an outcome improved after an intervention. However, a change occurring after a programme does not necessarily prove that the programme caused it. Other policies, economic conditions, demographic changes or external events may have contributed to the result. Impact evaluation seeks to establish a credible counterfactual: what would probably have happened to the same population in the absence of the intervention? This course introduces the scientific and statistical tools used to answer that question. Its content covers areas including: The definition and importance of impact evaluation; The attribution problem and the challenge of identifying causal effects; Randomized controlled trials and the role of random assignment; Problems that can arise during randomized evaluations; Statistical significance and margins of error; Analysis of data generated through randomized trials; Regression and its use in interpreting results; The relationship between sample size, statistical power and evaluation cost; Imperfect compliance with an experimental design; Missing data and its implications for analysis; and Quasi-experimental methods for situations in which randomization is not feasible. Learning objectives The official course information indicates that learners should be able to: Define impact evaluation and explain why it matters; Describe the importance of randomization and recognize common problems in randomized controlled trials; Identify statistical concepts and tools used in programme evaluation; Interpret regression concepts in the context of randomized-trial results; Explain the trade-off between sample size and the cost of a trial; and Describe the value and application of quasi-experimental methods. Free access and certificate information The World Bank Group s edX catalogue states that its courses can be audited free of charge and that learners may choose a verified certificate for a small fee. UN SDG lists this particular course as free and indicates that a certificate is available. These statements should not be read as a guarantee that the verified certificate itself is free. Learners should check the current price and certificate conditions displayed by edX before selecting a paid track. The course can be accessed through the official edX course page , with further details available on the UN SDG course listing . Resource 3: UNDP Microlearning on Measuring Good Systems Change The third component is What Is Good Systems Change and How Do We Measure It? , a UNDP microlearning resource written by Søren Vester Haldrup and published by UNDP Strategic Innovation. UN SDG correctly categorizes it as an English-language blog rather than a full course. The original article is presented as an approximately 16-minute read and includes a discussion summary, a session recording, questions and answers, and additional resources. The resource addresses a challenge that conventional monitoring and evaluation frameworks frequently struggle with: how to determine whether an entire system is changing in a desirable way when change is complex, non-linear and slow. Theme 1: Measuring change is not the same as evaluating change It is possible to observe that conditions are changing without determining whether the change is positive, negative, equitable or sustainable. Evaluation requires criteria against which change can be judged. The resource explores the use of evaluative rubrics, which describe standards for different levels of performance or change. Such rubrics can make judgments more transparent and provide a structured basis for discussion among programme teams, partners and decision-makers. They can also support learning by helping stakeholders examine what is changing, what may be driving the change and how strategy should be adapted. Theme 2: Measure what matters, not merely what is easy to count Organizations often rely heavily on quantitative key performance indicators because they are easy to aggregate and display. However, numbers alone may not explain whether relationships, incentives, institutional behaviour, public narratives or patterns of power are changing. The UNDP resource emphasizes the need to broaden the evidence base. Depending on the context, this may involve combining quantitative information with qualitative research, stakeholder perspectives, contextual data, ethnographic methods, storytelling and collective sensemaking. The aim is not to abandon numerical indicators, but to place them within a richer interpretation of how a system is evolving. Theme 3: Who decides what “good” change looks like? Judgments about desirable systems change are not neutral. Governments, donors, programme teams, communities and marginalized groups may define progress differently. If criteria are imposed only by those funding or managing an intervention, an evaluation may overlook the experiences and priorities of the people most affected. The resource therefore highlights inclusion and participation. People whom an initiative is intended to support should have a meaningful role in defining desired change, describing their lived experience and interpreting evidence. This makes evaluation more relevant and can reveal intended, unintended, positive and harmful consequences that standard indicators may miss. Additional practical insights The discussion also examines how organizations can balance long-term systems transformation with the need to track interim progress. Since major institutional or social change may take years, evaluators may need to monitor early signals such as changes in collaboration, public narratives, stakeholder participation, policy debate, learning or momentum. The resource further illustrates how rubrics, mixed methods and structured sensemaking can support adaptive management. Instead of using evaluation only as a retrospective accountability exercise, organizations can use evidence periodically to test assumptions, identify barriers and adjust their theories of change and strategies. Learners can access the consolidated UN SDG microlearning page or read the original UNDP Strategic Innovation article . How the three resources work together The strength of the pathway lies in its sequence. Each component answers a different evaluation question: Component Central question Main contribution UNIDO Evaluation Training How should an evaluation be understood, planned and managed? Evaluation principles, criteria, processes, stakeholder roles and management World Bank impact-evaluation course Did the policy or programme cause the observed result? Causal attribution, randomized trials, statistics, regression, sample size and quasi-experimental methods UNDP systems-change microlearning Is a complex system changing in a desirable and inclusive direction? Rubrics, mixed methods, interim signals, participation and systems-oriented learning Together, the resources help learners avoid three common mistakes: treating monitoring as evaluation, assuming correlation proves causation and reducing complex systems change to a narrow set of easy-to-count indicators. Key skills learners can develop Completing the full pathway can help learners strengthen their ability to: Frame evaluation purposes and questions clearly; Distinguish inputs, activities, outputs, outcomes and impacts; Separate monitoring functions from evaluative judgment; Understand how evaluations are commissioned, managed and used; Examine causal attribution rather than relying on before-and-after comparisons alone; Interpret introductory statistical concepts used in impact evaluation; Understand the design and limitations of randomized controlled trials; Recognize when quasi-experimental approaches may be appropriate; Assess long-term and interconnected systems change; Combine quantitative and qualitative evidence; Use rubrics and sensemaking to support learning and adaptation; Include affected stakeholders in defining and interpreting desirable change; and Translate evidence into stronger policy, programme and management decisions. Recommended order and study approach Learners can obtain the greatest value by following the pathway in its intended order: Begin with the UNIDO training. Its three-hour structure provides a manageable introduction to evaluation terminology, processes and management responsibilities. Proceed to the World Bank course. Allocate three to five hours each week and work through the statistical concepts carefully. Learners without a quantitative background may benefit from taking additional time to review examples and exercises. Complete the UNDP microlearning resource. Use it to reflect on the limits of conventional indicators and causal methods when dealing with interconnected systems and long-term transformation. Apply the learning to a real intervention. Select a policy, project or programme and draft evaluation questions, identify potential methods, consider a counterfactual and develop criteria for judging wider systems change. Maintain a learning record. Note important concepts, examples, methodological limitations and ways the material could improve current or future work. This is a recommended study strategy rather than a mandatory schedule established by the providers. Cost, certificates and important distinctions Learners should understand the access and credential arrangements before enrolling: UN SDG pathway: Free to access and organize the learning journey; no separate pathway certificate is stated on the official page. UNIDO Evaluation Training e-Learning: Free, approximately three hours and listed as providing no certificate. World Bank course on edX: Available for free audit; a verified certificate is available for a fee according to the World Bank Group s edX catalogue. Current pricing should be confirmed directly on edX. UNDP systems-change resource: Free microlearning blog and supporting material; it is not a certificate course. The pathway should therefore be promoted as a free learning opportunity, but not as three free certificate courses. Application deadline No fixed application or enrolment deadline is stated on the official UN SDG pathway or the individual resource pages as of 10 August 2026. The two courses are described as self-paced, while the UNDP resource is available on demand. Learners can begin while the pages and registration options remain active. Because online-course availability, platform policies and certificate prices can change, prospective learners should verify the current status on the official pages before enrolling or paying for a credential. How to enrol and access the pathway Follow these steps: Visit the official Evaluation for Sustainable Development learning pathway . Create a UN SDG account or sign in to an existing account. Select the option to enrol in the learning pathway. Open the UNIDO course and follow the registration links for its three modules. Open the World Bank course and create or use an edX account to enrol. Review the difference between free audit access and the optional verified-certificate track. Read the UNDP systems-change microlearning article and use the accompanying recording, questions and supporting resources where available. Complete the components in sequence and apply the concepts to a practical evaluation problem. Conclusion The UN SDG Evaluation for Sustainable Development pathway offers a well-structured introduction to three levels of evaluation practice. UNIDO s training explains the foundations and management of evaluation. The World Bank Group course develops an understanding of causal impact measurement through experimental, statistical and quasi-experimental methods. UNDP s microlearning resource then expands the discussion to complex systems, where progress must be interpreted through mixed evidence, participation, rubrics and ongoing learning. For learners seeking to understand how evidence can improve policies and programmes, the pathway provides substantial value without requiring payment for access to the learning materials. Its greatest benefit comes from completing all three components and applying the concepts to real decisions rather than treating completion or certification as the final objective. title: Commonwealth Leaders Academy Programmes Associate Volunteer Opportunity: Remote Role with £100 Monthly Stipend
summary: Are you looking for a remote volunteer opportunity that can help you gain practical experience in programme management, communications, leadership development and international affairs? The Commonwealth Leaders Academy (CLA) is inviting applications for a Programmes Associate (Volunteer) to support the planning and delivery of its programmes and activities. This remote opportunity is particularly relevant to organised, proactive and creative individuals who want to develop their professional experience while contributing to initiatives focused on youth leadership, capacity building, policy engagement and international collaboration. The selected volunteer will work closely with the Commonwealth Leaders Academy to provide operational, administrative and communications support across its programmes. The position offers practical exposure to international development and leadership programmes, opportunities to build a professional network, a potential professional reference and a monthly stipend of £100 to help cover incidental volunteering costs. Commonwealth Leaders Academy Programmes Associate Volunteer Opportunity The Programmes Associate (Volunteer) will play a supporting role in the implementation of CLA s programmes and activities. The position combines programme coordination, administration, communications and digital content responsibilities, making it suitable for individuals who want to build a broad set of transferable professional skills. The role is conducted remotely , allowing the successful volunteer to contribute without being required to work from a physical CLA office. The initial appointment is for one month , with the possibility of renewal depending on programme requirements, performance and mutual agreement. Opportunity Details Organisation: Commonwealth Leaders Academy (CLA) Position: Programmes Associate (Volunteer) Location: Remote Position Type: Volunteer Initial Duration: One month Renewability: The appointment may be renewed Expected Commitment: Up to 20 hours per week, depending on programme needs and availability Monthly Stipend: £100 Work Areas: Programme support, administration, communications, events, social media and promotional content Application Deadline: No deadline is stated in the provided opportunity information About the Commonwealth Leaders Academy The Commonwealth Leaders Academy is a Community Interest Company focused on developing the next generation of Commonwealth leaders. The organisation works in areas including leadership development, capacity building, policy engagement and international collaboration. Through partnerships with governments, youth organisations, universities and development partners, CLA develops and delivers programmes designed to empower young people to contribute to positive change within their communities and across the wider Commonwealth. The organisation s work provides volunteers with the opportunity to gain exposure to initiatives involving youth development, leadership, international affairs and programme delivery. For someone seeking early-career experience in these fields, supporting CLA s programmes can provide an opportunity to understand how programmes and initiatives are coordinated, communicated and delivered. About the Programmes Associate Volunteer Role The Programmes Associate will provide operational and administrative assistance to CLA s programmes and activities. The position is designed for someone who is organised, dependable, proactive and creative. Because the role combines several functions, the successful volunteer should be comfortable handling different responsibilities and switching between administrative, programme and communications tasks. The position may be particularly valuable for individuals interested in developing careers in: Programme management Project coordination Communications Digital communications International development Youth development Leadership programmes Non-governmental organisations Civil society International affairs Event coordination Public engagement Social media and digital content Rather than focusing on one specialised function, the role provides exposure to several areas of programme implementation. Key Responsibilities of the Programmes Associate The volunteer will support CLA across two major areas: programme support and communications . 1. Programme Support The Programmes Associate will assist with the planning, coordination and implementation of CLA programmes and events. Responsibilities may include: Supporting the planning of programmes and events. Assisting with programme coordination activities. Helping prepare programme materials. Supporting the preparation of reports and documentation. Drafting routine correspondence. Preparing and sending follow-up emails where required. Assisting with administrative tasks related to programme delivery. Supporting other operational activities connected to CLA initiatives. These responsibilities can help the volunteer develop an understanding of how programmes move from planning to implementation. Programme support experience can also be valuable for individuals who intend to pursue careers in project management, development work, youth programming, nonprofit management or international organisations. 2. Communications Support Communications form another important component of the role. The Programmes Associate will assist with CLA s communication and promotional activities, including: Designing presentation slides. Preparing briefing materials. Supporting the development of social media content. Scheduling social media posts. Assisting with newsletters. Supporting announcements. Helping prepare promotional materials. Contributing to other routine communications activities. This aspect of the role can be particularly useful for individuals with an interest in communications, digital marketing, public relations, social media management, content creation or advocacy. Candidates who already have experience using tools such as Canva, PowerPoint or other presentation and design platforms may be able to apply their existing skills while developing new professional capabilities. Skills and Qualifications Required The Commonwealth Leaders Academy is seeking candidates who can demonstrate strong communication, organisation and digital working skills. Essential Requirements Applicants should have: Excellent Written and Verbal Communication Skills Strong communication skills are important because the role involves drafting correspondence, preparing communications materials, assisting with newsletters and supporting programme-related activities. The successful volunteer should be able to communicate information clearly, professionally and accurately. Strong Organisation and Time Management The role may involve multiple responsibilities at the same time. Applicants should therefore be capable of organising their workload, meeting agreed deadlines and prioritising tasks effectively. Good time management will be particularly important given that programme activities and communications tasks may occur simultaneously. High Attention to Detail Attention to detail is essential when preparing programme documentation, reports, presentations, emails, social media content and other communications materials. Ability to Work Independently Because the position is remote, the successful volunteer should be comfortable working independently. Microsoft Office and Google Workspace Skills Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Google Workspace is required. Relevant tools may include applications used for: Document preparation Spreadsheets Presentations Email and communication File sharing Collaborative working Online document management Familiarity with these tools can make it easier for the volunteer to participate effectively in a remote working environment. Canva or PowerPoint Experience Applicants should have experience using Canva or PowerPoint to create presentations. Interest in Leadership and International Affairs The role may also appeal to individuals interested in leadership development, international affairs, policy engagement and international cooperation. Experience with Youth Organisations, NGOs or Student Organisations Experience working with youth organisations, NGOs or student organisations is desirable. Time Commitment The Programmes Associate volunteer position is designed to be flexible. This means candidates should be prepared to contribute regularly to agreed activities while balancing their other professional, academic or personal responsibilities. Because the position is remote, applicants should also ensure that they have sufficient time and a reliable working environment to complete assigned responsibilities. Volunteer Stipend Although this is a volunteer position, selected volunteers will receive a monthly stipend of £100 . The stipend is intended to contribute towards incidental costs associated with volunteering. It is important to understand that the £100 payment is not a salary or wage . The position remains a volunteer role, with the stipend intended to help offset expenses that may arise from participating in the programme. Benefits of the Commonwealth Leaders Academy Volunteer Opportunity The Programmes Associate position offers several potential professional and career development benefits. 1. Gain International Programme Experience Volunteers will have an opportunity to contribute to programmes connected with leadership development, youth empowerment, capacity building and international collaboration. This can provide practical experience that may strengthen a future CV or professional portfolio. 2. Develop Programme Management Skills By assisting with programme planning, coordination, documentation and reporting, volunteers can develop practical programme management and administrative skills. These skills can be useful when applying for future internships, fellowships, programme assistant positions, project coordination roles and development-sector opportunities. 3. Strengthen Communications Skills The role involves several communications responsibilities, including social media content, newsletters, announcements, presentations and promotional materials. This can help volunteers develop a stronger communications portfolio. 4. Build a Global Professional Network The position provides an opportunity to interact with people involved in leadership, youth development, international development and related areas. Developing professional relationships through such experiences can be valuable for future career and collaboration opportunities. 5. Receive a Professional Reference A professional reference may be provided based on satisfactory performance. A positive reference can be useful when applying for future employment, internships, fellowships, volunteer roles or academic opportunities. 6. Contribute to High-Profile Initiatives Volunteers will have the opportunity to contribute to CLA initiatives and activities. This can provide practical exposure to the processes involved in delivering programmes and communicating their work to wider audiences. 7. Work Remotely The remote nature of the opportunity provides flexibility for individuals who may not be able to relocate or commute to an office. Remote work can also help volunteers develop important digital collaboration, communication and self-management skills. Who Should Apply? This opportunity may be particularly suitable for individuals who are interested in building careers or experience in programme management, communications, youth development and international development. Potential applicants include: Recent graduates seeking practical professional experience. Students with relevant skills and interests. Early-career professionals looking to expand their programme and communications experience. Communications and marketing professionals seeking experience in the development sector. Individuals interested in youth leadership programmes. People interested in international development and international affairs. Volunteers with experience supporting NGOs or community organisations. Individuals with experience in student or youth organisations. Candidates with Canva, PowerPoint and social media skills. Organised individuals who can work independently in a remote environment. Why This Opportunity Could Be Valuable for Early-Career Professionals Breaking into international development, programme management and communications can be challenging because many entry-level positions require previous experience. A role such as the CLA Programmes Associate position can provide practical exposure to several areas at once. For example, a volunteer may gain experience in programme coordination while also developing communications skills through social media, newsletters and presentation design. This combination can be particularly valuable for candidates who want to build a versatile professional profile. Show That You Can Work Remotely Since this is a remote position, candidates should demonstrate their ability to: Work independently. Communicate effectively online. Meet deadlines.
