title: IPPF Youth Networker Position in Malaysia 2026: Apply for a Three-Year Youth Leadership and SRHR Role
summary: The International Planned Parenthood Federation is accepting applications for a Youth Networker position based in Malaysia. This full-time, fixed-term opportunity is designed as a career-development role for someone interested in youth leadership, sexual and reproductive health and rights, comprehensive sexuality education, advocacy, social justice, and inclusive international development. The successful applicant will help strengthen meaningful youth participation throughout IPPF’s East, South East Asia and Oceania Region. The position will connect young people with regional and global platforms, support youth-led accountability, amplify youth voices within the Federation, and help IPPF Member Associations develop programmes and services that respond effectively to young people’s needs. IPPF describes the opportunity as a stepping-stone development role for someone beginning a career in the sector. The appointment is anticipated to last three years, during which the successful applicant will gain experience working with youth networks, regional teams, Member Associations, advocates, programme specialists, and other Youth Networkers across the Federation. Applications must be submitted by 18 August 2026 through the official IPPF recruitment portal . Key Information About the IPPF Youth Networker Position Organization: International Planned Parenthood Federation Position title: Youth Networker Location: Malaysia Regional coverage: East, South East Asia and Oceania Employment schedule: Full-time Contract type: Fixed-term Anticipated contract duration: Three years Application deadline: 18 August 2026 Required application documents: CV or résumé and a short cover letter Optional document: Relevant work sample Application platform: IPPF’s Personio recruitment portal The vacancy announcement does not provide a salary range, employment grade, starting date, relocation package, remote-working arrangement, or details of visa sponsorship. Applicants should avoid making assumptions about these conditions and seek clarification from IPPF if shortlisted. About the International Planned Parenthood Federation The International Planned Parenthood Federation, commonly known as IPPF, is a global movement working to advance sexual and reproductive health, rights, healthcare access, bodily autonomy, gender equality, and social justice. IPPF operates through a worldwide network of Member Associations and partners. These organizations deliver healthcare services, support communities, provide comprehensive sexuality education, advocate for legal and policy reforms, and promote the rights of people who face barriers to accessing sexual and reproductive healthcare. The Federation describes itself as a diverse, feminist, values-driven, multinational, multicultural, multiracial, multilingual, and intergenerational workplace. Its work places particular emphasis on communities affected by marginalization, exclusion, stigma, inequality, poverty, discrimination, humanitarian emergencies, and limited access to healthcare. IPPF’s Strategy 2028 is built around four broad pillars: centring care on people, advancing the sexuality agenda, building solidarity for change, and strengthening the Federation. Young people and marginalized communities are intended to play a central role in that strategy rather than simply being treated as passive recipients of services. IPPF’s official Strategy 2028 announcement explains the Federation’s commitment to transformation driven by young people. Why IPPF Is Recruiting a Youth Networker IPPF is recruiting the Youth Networker to strengthen the direct participation of young people in its regional and global work. The position is not limited to communicating with young people or promoting activities on social media. It is intended to embed meaningful youth participation in organizational decision-making, programme development, governance, advocacy, service delivery, monitoring, evaluation, and accountability. The Youth Networker will help ensure that young people can: Influence decisions that affect their health, rights, and communities. Participate directly in the design of programmes and services. Contribute to implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and organizational learning. Hold institutions and decision-makers accountable for youth-related commitments. Develop regional and global networks for activism and collaboration. Build leadership skills and gain access to mentoring and growth opportunities. Shape sexual and reproductive health services so that they are accessible, respectful, responsive, and youth-friendly. Participate in advocacy for comprehensive sexuality education and sexual and reproductive health and rights. IPPF’s East, South East Asia and Oceania regional work recognizes that young people experience different barriers depending on factors such as poverty, disability, gender, sexuality, geography, social exclusion, and access to services. The organization’s regional publications emphasize youth-led and youth-centred programming as a major element of Strategy 2028. IPPF’s regional update on youth-centred programming provides additional context for this approach. Primary Purpose of the Position The central purpose of the Youth Networker position is to promote youth-centred action across IPPF’s East, South East Asia and Oceania Region while connecting young people to the Federation’s wider global community. The successful applicant will work to ensure that young people meaningfully influence: Organizational decision-making Governance processes Programme planning Programme implementation Advocacy campaigns Healthcare and service delivery Monitoring and evaluation Organizational development Regional and global youth forums Youth-related commitments under IPPF Strategy 2028 Meaningful youth engagement in this context goes beyond inviting young people to attend meetings. It requires creating structures through which young people can express their views safely, participate in decisions, lead programmes, evaluate results, question existing practices, and hold organizations accountable. Detailed Responsibilities of the IPPF Youth Networker 1. Develop and Strengthen Regional Youth Networks The Youth Networker will help organize youth action across the region and contribute to the development of an inclusive IPPF youth network. Responsibilities will include: Supporting established regional youth networks to develop and implement their plans. Helping create youth networks in locations where effective structures do not already exist. Promoting participation by young people from marginalized and underrepresented communities. Connecting national and local youth structures with regional and global platforms. Encouraging collaboration between young people working in different countries and social contexts. Helping regional youth networks align their activities with IPPF Strategy 2028. Building momentum around youth leadership, activism, accountability, and movement development. The successful candidate will need to understand that youth groups are not uniform. Different participants will have different identities, experiences, access requirements, languages, priorities, and levels of power. Inclusive network building will therefore be a central responsibility. 2. Promote Youth-Led Accountability The position will advise IPPF’s regional structures and Member Associations on how to involve young people directly in accountability processes. This may involve helping young people: Examine whether organizations are meeting their commitments. Participate in programme reviews. Comment on the quality and accessibility of services. Contribute to monitoring and evaluation activities. Identify gaps between organizational commitments and actual implementation. Present recommendations to decision-makers. Follow up on actions promised by institutions or programme leaders. Youth-led accountability means that young people should have practical ways to assess programmes and influence improvements, rather than being asked for opinions without receiving meaningful responses. 3. Support Regional and Global Youth Forums The Youth Networker will oversee or contribute to IPPF’s Regional Youth Forums and Global Youth Forums. This work could include: Supporting the planning and coordination of forums. Encouraging inclusive participation. Helping participants prepare for discussions and decision-making. Connecting forum outcomes to IPPF programmes and organizational processes. Following up on recommendations and commitments. Ensuring that the voices of marginalized participants are not overlooked. Supporting communication between regional and global youth structures. Experience organizing meetings, consultations, workshops, youth events, campaigns, or collaborative projects would therefore be particularly relevant. 4. Integrate Youth Participation Throughout the Programme Cycle The Youth Networker will promote meaningful youth engagement throughout the complete programme cycle. Young people should be able to participate in: Identifying community needs and priorities. Designing programmes and services. Planning activities and implementation strategies. Delivering youth-led or youth-centred initiatives. Monitoring progress. Evaluating results. Sharing lessons and recommendations. Improving future programmes. Applicants should understand participatory approaches and be able to help teams move from symbolic consultation to genuine collaboration with young people. 5. Strengthen Youth Leadership and Activism The successful applicant will contribute to leadership development by identifying and recommending opportunities for young people within the Federation. This responsibility includes: Identifying promising youth leaders and activists. Promoting leadership pathways within regional networks. Developing or recommending mentoring approaches. Connecting young people with learning and development opportunities. Encouraging participation in advocacy and movement-building. Helping young people build confidence, knowledge, networks, and practical leadership experience. Creating stronger connections between IPPF youth networks and wider youth movements. The role is therefore suitable for someone who can encourage others, build trust, coordinate diverse participants, and create opportunities without dominating youth-led spaces. 6. Amplify Youth Voices Within the IPPF Secretariat The Youth Networker will act as a champion for youth-centred action within the IPPF Secretariat. This means helping the organization listen to and act on young people’s perspectives. The successful applicant will work to ensure that youth voices inform internal discussions, regional priorities, programmes, advocacy, services, and organizational development. The role will also contribute to creating safe environments that: Encourage young people to participate openly. Respect different identities and experiences. Promote diversity and inclusion. Challenge racism and structural inequality. Protect people from harm. Safeguard organizational finances and resources. Support responsible, transparent, and accountable decision-making. 7. Support IPPF Member Associations IPPF Member Associations are nationally based organizations that carry out much of the Federation’s work within individual countries and communities. The Youth Networker will support these associations to: Establish or strengthen local youth networks. Develop youth-centred programmes. Design youth-led initiatives. Improve youth participation in organizational structures. Deliver youth-friendly healthcare and information. Improve access to sexual and reproductive health services. Make services more responsive to young people’s realities. Monitor youth-related indicators and commitments. Advance comprehensive sexuality education. Strengthen accountability to young people. The vacancy also refers to collaboration with colleagues described as “Architects of Cooperation” and with regional staff working in Membership Support and Development and External Relations. 8. Advance Youth-Centred Care and Youth-Friendly Services A significant part of the role will involve helping Member Associations strengthen services intended for young people. Youth-friendly services should consider issues such as: Confidentiality Privacy Respect Accessibility Affordability Non-discrimination Informed choice Bodily autonomy Age-appropriate communication Responsiveness to diverse identities Protection from stigma or judgment Safe referral and safeguarding procedures The Youth Networker will not simply promote the existence of services. The position will help assess whether those services are accessible, appropriate, high-quality, and genuinely responsive to young people. 9. Support Comprehensive Sexuality Education Comprehensive Sexuality Education, abbreviated as CSE, is specifically identified in the vacancy as an important area under IPPF Strategy 2028. The successful applicant may support efforts that help young people access accurate, rights-based, inclusive, and age-appropriate information about: Sexual and reproductive health Relationships Consent Gender Bodily autonomy Sexual and reproductive rights Diversity Violence prevention Healthcare and support services Informed decision-making Applicants should be comfortable representing IPPF’s position on comprehensive sexuality education and broader sexual and reproductive health and rights. 10. Collect and Analyze Evidence The role includes a learning and evidence component. The Youth Networker will be expected to collect, analyze, and share information concerning: Youth participation Youth-centred programmes Youth-led accountability Youth-friendly services Effective engagement methods Good practices Programme results Lessons learned Challenges experienced by Member Associations Approaches that could be adapted across the region The objective is to help IPPF continuously improve its work rather than treating youth engagement as an isolated activity. 11. Monitor Strategy 2028 Commitments The Youth Networker will contribute to monitoring and reporting on youth-related indicators and organizational commitments under IPPF Strategy 2028. This may require the successful candidate to: Coordinate information from different teams. Follow up with Member Associations. Review qualitative and quantitative evidence. Identify implementation gaps. Help prepare reports or presentations. Share lessons across countries and regional networks. Recommend practical improvements. Track whether youth-related commitments are producing meaningful results. Strong organization, analytical thinking, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate evidence clearly will be valuable. 12. Complete Additional Responsibilities Like many regional positions, the Youth Networker may be asked to undertake other duties assigned by the line manager according to changing organizational priorities and operational needs. Applicants should therefore be adaptable and willing to contribute beyond narrowly defined tasks when necessary. Rotating Team-Leadership Responsibility The vacancy explains that one of IPPF’s Youth Networker roles will serve as Team Leader and will have dual reporting to the Regional Director chairing youth-related work. The team-lead responsibility is intended to rotate to promote equal opportunities. This arrangement may allow different Youth Networkers to develop coordination, leadership, reporting, and team-support experience during their appointments. Skills and Experience IPPF Is Seeking IPPF has identified several essential skills and personal qualities for the position. Commitment to IPPF’s Mission Applicants should be informed and passionate about IPPF’s work. They must be comfortable advocating for the organization’s positions on sexual and reproductive health, rights, justice, bodily autonomy, gender equality, comprehensive sexuality education, and inclusion. Experience Working With Youth Groups Relevant experience may come from employment, volunteering, activism, student leadership, community organizing, peer education, advocacy, youth networks, nonprofit programmes, or similar activities. Applicants should be able to demonstrate how they have: Worked constructively with young people. Helped individuals or groups express their views. Amplified underrepresented voices. Organized activities or networks. Supported participation in decision-making. Built safe and inclusive spaces. Connected youth priorities with institutional processes. Cross-Cultural Communication The position requires an ability to relate positively and respectfully to people from different cultures and backgrounds. Because the role covers a diverse international region, applicants should demonstrate cultural sensitivity, curiosity, active listening, inclusive communication, and a willingness to learn from people with experiences different from their own. Coordination and Organization Applicants should possess good: Time-management skills Coordination abilities Organizational skills Follow-up practices Meeting or event-planning abilities Communication skills Task-prioritization skills The successful candidate may need to manage several relationships, activities, deadlines, and regional priorities simultaneously. Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills IPPF expects the Youth Networker to analyze evidence, identify challenges, recommend improvements, and help teams respond to barriers affecting youth participation and service access. Applicants should use examples that demonstrate their ability to understand a problem, consult relevant people, develop a practical response, and evaluate the result. Digital Competence Applicants must be competent in: Microsoft Office Social media platforms Digital communication Preparing documents and presentations Supporting online engagement and collaboration Social media experience is relevant, but the position involves much more than content creation. Applicants should demonstrate how digital platforms can support participation, networking, advocacy, learning, or the amplification of youth voices. English-Language Ability The vacancy lists “Business English Preliminary” ability across writing, reading, and speaking as an essential requirement. The application portal allows applications to be submitted in English, Arabic, French, or Spanish. However, applicants should remember that the job description specifically identifies business-level English ability as necessary for the position. Inclusive and Curious Working Style IPPF is looking for someone who is: Inclusive Curious Open to other people’s ideas Able to develop original ideas Comfortable articulating those ideas Respectful of different perspectives Willing to learn and adapt Lived Experience The vacancy states that lived experience of belonging to a marginalized group is considered an asset. It is not presented as an absolute requirement. IPPF also encourages applications from people with lived experience and from the communities it serves, particularly people from marginalized groups. Safeguarding Responsibilities Safeguarding is a central requirement of the Youth Networker position because the role involves work connected to young people and potentially vulnerable adults. The successful candidate must: Understand the importance of safeguarding. Act as a positive safeguarding role model. Follow safeguarding reporting procedures. Support safe participation. Respond appropriately to concerns. Sign and comply with IPPF’s Code of Conduct. Sign and comply with IPPF’s Safeguarding Policy for Children and Vulnerable Adults. Cooperate with applicable background and safeguarding checks. IPPF defines safeguarding as protecting children and vulnerable adults from harm that could arise through contact with its staff, volunteers, programmes, partners, or activities. Its policy covers prevention, reporting, and organizational response. Further details are available through IPPF’s safeguarding information and reporting page . The application portal states that appointments are subject to relevant safeguarding and background checks. These can include identity, employment history, qualification, reference, criminal-record, and other checks permitted under applicable laws. IPPF also recognizes that some candidates may have past convictions connected to activism or identity and states that these are not automatically considered a barrier to employment. IPPF’s Values and Workplace Ethos The successful applicant must be able to work in a way that reflects IPPF’s stated values. These include: Upholding dignity and bodily autonomy. Advancing sexual and reproductive rights. Promoting equality through feminist, anti-racist, anti-ableist, and intersectional practice. Challenging structural inequalities. Supporting social movements for justice. Recognizing sexual and reproductive health as a positive state of well-being. Building global and local communities led by those most affected. Acting with integrity and accountability. Learning, adapting, and remaining resilient in complex environments. Applicants must also be comfortable working within an organization that is feminist, pro-choice, supportive of safe abortion access, supportive of people regardless of sexual orientation or gender identity and expression, and supportive of healthcare access and rights in relation to sex work. Candidates should assess this values alignment honestly because representing and upholding these positions is an important part of the role. Professional Development and Potential Value of the Role IPPF presents the position as a development opportunity for someone beginning a career in the sector. Potential professional-development value includes: Experience within an international Federation. Exposure to regional and global youth networks. Practical involvement in sexual and reproductive health and rights. Experience supporting international programmes. Participation in regional and global youth forums. Opportunities to strengthen advocacy and movement-building skills. Experience with monitoring, evaluation, evidence collection, and reporting. Cross-cultural collaboration. Experience supporting Member Associations. Potential rotating team-lead responsibilities. Mentoring and leadership-development exposure. A pathway toward future roles within IPPF, its Member Associations, partner organizations, or the wider international-development sector. IPPF states that it hopes people completing the anticipated three-year appointment will progress to other opportunities within the Federation or beyond it. This is an organizational aspiration, not a guarantee of another position. Why Consider Working With IPPF? According to the vacancy announcement, IPPF offers meaningful work, professional development, an international working environment, and an opportunity to contribute to lasting social impact. The organization highlights work addressing: Maternal mortality Unintended pregnancies Gender-based violence Comprehensive sexuality education Sexual and reproductive healthcare Sexual and reproductive rights and justice Access barriers affecting marginalized communities Gender equality Racism and structural inequality IPPF also emphasizes its global reach, commitment to diversity and inclusion, and mission-driven approach. The vacancy does not list monetary benefits, insurance, leave entitlements, allowances, retirement benefits, relocation support, or a salary range. Applicants should distinguish the organization’s broad professional value proposition from specific contractual benefits, which would need to be confirmed during recruitment. Application Documents Applicants must prepare the following documents: 1. CV or Résumé A CV or résumé is mandatory and must not exceed two pages. It should highlight: Relevant youth engagement experience Advocacy or activism Programme coordination Network development Community engagement Monitoring and evaluation Evidence collection Social media and digital communication Cross-cultural collaboration Safeguarding experience Training relevant to sexual and reproductive health and rights Measurable achievements 2. Short Cover Letter A cover letter is also mandatory. It should explain, in the applicant’s own words: Why the position is of interest. How the applicant’s skills match the role. Which experiences demonstrate suitability. What achievements are relevant. Why the applicant supports IPPF’s mission and values. How the applicant would contribute to youth participation and leadership. 3. Optional Work Sample Applicants may upload a work sample, although it is not mandatory. A relevant sample could include: A youth-engagement strategy A campaign plan A workshop guide An advocacy product A research or learning brief A monitoring report A communications product A youth-network activity plan Applicants should only submit work they are authorized to share and should remove confidential or personally identifiable information. The combined upload size for the CV, cover letter, and any optional work sample must not exceed 20 MB. Information Required on the Application Form The public application form requests information covering: Legal first and last name Preferred name Preferred pronouns Location Phone number Email address Current country of residence Permanent country of residence, if different Preferred contact time and method LinkedIn profile, if available Current employer Current job title Work-permit requirements Previous work with IPPF, if applicable Employment history Relevant non-employment experience Years of experience Relevant qualifications or training Languages and proficiency levels Availability to start Expected salary Criminal convictions or pending proceedings Up to three references Nationality or nationalities Interview adjustments or special arrangements The form also invites applicants to discuss volunteering, activism, learning, parenting, self-care, and other relevant experiences. This indicates that IPPF is prepared to consider experience gained outside conventional paid employment. Written Application Questions Applicants should be prepared to answer questions covering: What sexual and reproductive health and rights mean to them. Their comfort representing and supporting IPPF’s mission. Their motivation for applying. How their experience and skills fit the position. How they would uphold IPPF’s feminist, pro-choice, pro-sex, anti-racist, and safeguarding values. Any gaps in their professional history. The motivation response has a stated limit of approximately 200 to 250 words. The values and safeguarding response is displayed with a maximum of 250 characters, so applicants should prepare a particularly concise answer for that field. References and Background Checks The form asks applicants to provide up to three references who can comment on their work, skills, or suitability. Applicants should: Select people who know their work well. Ask for permission before listing them. Provide accurate and current contact information. Brief references on the role. Choose referees who can discuss youth engagement, leadership, safeguarding, advocacy, coordination, or other relevant experience. Shortlisted or selected candidates may be subject to reference, identity, employment-history, qualification, safeguarding, criminal-record, and other legally permitted checks. How to Apply for the IPPF Youth Networker Position Read the complete official IPPF Youth Networker vacancy . Review IPPF’s mission, Strategy 2028, safeguarding expectations, and organizational values. Prepare a targeted CV or résumé of no more than two pages. Write a concise cover letter connecting your experience directly to the responsibilities and essential skills. Prepare clear examples of youth engagement, advocacy, network building, programme participation, evidence use, or safeguarding. Gather accurate information about your employment history, qualifications, language proficiency, availability, expected salary, work-permit needs, and references. Draft the written application responses before entering them into the portal. Explain any gaps in your professional history. If there are none, the portal instructs applicants to enter “N/A.” Upload the mandatory CV and cover letter. Add an optional work sample only if it strengthens the application. Review every section for accuracy and completeness. Submit the application through the official online application form . Save the submission confirmation for personal records. Application Tips Demonstrate Meaningful Youth Engagement Avoid simply stating that you are passionate about young people. Provide an example showing how young people influenced a decision, programme, campaign, service, or organizational process through your work. Show How You Amplified Voices Explain how you created opportunities for underrepresented people to express their priorities and how those contributions affected the final outcome. Include Experience Beyond Paid Employment Relevant activism, volunteering, peer education, student leadership, community organizing, caregiving, independent learning, and lived experience may strengthen the application. Connect Experience to IPPF Strategy 2028 Show that you understand the relationship between youth leadership, youth-centred care, comprehensive sexuality education, accountability, advocacy, and sexual and reproductive health and rights. Address Safeguarding Directly Include a practical example of how you protected confidentiality, managed risk, created a safe environment, followed a reporting procedure, or responded appropriately to a concern. Demonstrate Values Alignment Applicants should provide specific evidence that they can work respectfully within a feminist, pro-choice, anti-racist, inclusive, and rights-based organization. Quantify Achievements Where Possible Instead of writing that you “supported a youth network,” explain the scale and outcome. For example, state how many participants, organizations, communities, events, or countries were involved and what changed because of the activity. Tailor the CV A two-page limit requires careful prioritization. Focus on experiences and achievements directly connected to: Youth participation Network development Advocacy Leadership Programme coordination Monitoring and evaluation Data and learning Inclusive communication Safeguarding Sexual and reproductive health and rights Application Deadline The official closing date is 18 August 2026 . title: UK Government Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026: Applications Open for Young People to Help Shape Climate and Nature Policy
summary: Applications are now open for the UK Government Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026 , a new national initiative designed to give young people a meaningful voice in shaping government thinking on climate change, nature recovery, clean energy and wider environmental policy. The UK Government is recruiting 15 young people aged 16 to 25 from across the United Kingdom to become members of its first Youth Climate and Nature Panel. The initiative will create a direct channel through which young people from different backgrounds, communities and experiences can share their perspectives with government and contribute to conversations about some of the most important environmental challenges facing current and future generations. Importantly, applicants do not need to be climate scientists, environmental campaigners or policy experts. The government is seeking young people with different experiences and relationships with climate, nature and the environment, including those who may never previously have participated in environmental organisations, protests or government consultations. Applications for the Youth Climate and Nature Panel close on Friday, 11 September 2026. About the UK Government Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026 The Youth Climate and Nature Panel is a new national initiative that will bring together 15 young people between the ages of 16 and 25 from across the UK. The panel is intended to ensure that young people s experiences, concerns and ideas are better represented in government thinking about climate and nature policy. Decisions being made today about climate change, biodiversity, clean energy, nature restoration, food systems, employment and environmental protection will have consequences lasting for decades. Today s younger generations will therefore live with many of the long-term outcomes of these decisions. The Youth Climate and Nature Panel seeks to provide young people with an opportunity to participate in those discussions rather than simply hearing about policies after decisions have already been made. Panel members will be expected to: Share their views and experiences with government. Provide insights and advice on climate and nature issues. Help government understand how environmental policies affect young people and their communities. Strengthen engagement between government and younger generations. Encourage collaboration between different generations. Contribute ideas about climate, nature, energy and environmental priorities. Help identify issues that young people believe deserve greater attention. Support broader conversations about building a fair and sustainable future. A particularly important feature of the panel is that members will have an opportunity to help determine their own priorities. Rather than having every subject decided for them, panel members will have space to identify and explore the climate and nature issues they believe matter most. Why Has the Youth Climate and Nature Panel Been Created? Climate change, biodiversity loss, environmental degradation and the transition toward cleaner energy systems are long-term challenges. Young people will inherit the consequences of decisions being made today, making their participation particularly important. At the same time, young people are already contributing solutions in their schools, workplaces, families and local communities. They bring experiences and perspectives that may differ significantly depending on where they live, their education, employment, community and relationship with the natural environment. The UK Government therefore wants to create more meaningful opportunities for younger people to contribute to policymaking. The Youth Climate and Nature Panel is intended to move beyond simply communicating government policies to young people. Instead, it creates an avenue through which young people can contribute perspectives that may help inform government thinking. Background to the Youth Climate and Nature Panel The Youth Climate and Nature Panel was initially announced by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero in December 2025 as part of Energising Britain: Your Voice in Our Clean Energy Superpower Mission . Its development forms part of a wider government commitment to involve communities in climate and nature policymaking. This approach is also reflected in the government s Environmental Improvement Plan . The underlying principle is that effective environmental policy can benefit from involving people and communities during the policymaking process rather than expecting them only to respond after major decisions have already been made. The new Youth Climate and Nature Panel will extend this participatory approach specifically to younger generations. What Will Youth Climate and Nature Panel Members Do? The 15 successful applicants will have the opportunity to bring young people s experiences and perspectives into conversations with government. Their role is expected to include sharing views, providing advice and insight, strengthening youth engagement and helping promote collaboration between generations. One of the most significant elements of the initiative is that members will help decide what issues the panel prioritises. This means the panel s agenda could reflect environmental concerns that its young members believe are particularly important to their generation and communities. Potential subjects could include: Nature restoration Members may consider how nature can be restored and protected throughout the UK, including questions surrounding biodiversity, habitats and long-term nature recovery. Climate change adaptation As communities experience the effects of a changing climate, the panel could consider how the country prepares for and adapts to those changes. Access to nature Discussions could examine opportunities to improve people s ability to access and benefit from natural environments. Environmental quality Panel members may explore broader questions about creating and maintaining a healthier natural environment. Clean energy transition The transition away from higher-carbon energy sources toward cleaner alternatives is expected to transform communities, industries and employment. Young people could provide perspectives on what this transition means for their generation. Sustainable food systems The relationship between food production, agriculture, environmental protection and sustainability could also feature in the panel s work. Circular economy Panel discussions could examine ways of reducing waste, reusing resources and developing economic systems that use materials more efficiently. Green jobs and careers The transition toward a cleaner economy is expected to create and transform employment opportunities. Panel members could consider what green careers, skills and emerging technologies mean for young people s futures. The final priorities will not necessarily be limited to these subjects. Panel members will have an opportunity to influence the issues they believe deserve attention. Who Can Apply for the Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026? Applications are open to young people aged 16 to 25 who are based anywhere in the United Kingdom . The government is particularly interested in receiving applications from young people with a wide variety of backgrounds, interests, experiences and relationships with climate, nature and the environment. Applicants might, for example, be interested in: How farmers and agricultural communities are helping restore nature. How renewable energy developments affect local communities. How towns and cities can become greener. How communities can become more resilient to climate change. How clean energy will affect the country s future. How green careers will change employment opportunities. How emerging environmental technologies could influence the economy. How young people can participate in environmental decision-making. How nature and biodiversity can be protected and restored. How government decisions concerning climate and nature affect everyday life. However, previous involvement in these areas is not a requirement . Find out more and apply to join the Youth Climate and Nature Panel. You Do Not Need to Be a Climate or Environmental Expert One of the most important aspects of this opportunity is its accessibility to young people who may not have formal environmental experience. Applicants do not need to be policy experts . They also do not need to have previously joined an environmental organisation, participated in a climate protest or spoken with government representatives. The government has specifically indicated that it also wants to hear from young people who may never have participated in those activities. This means applicants should not assume they are unqualified simply because they lack formal experience in environmental advocacy or policymaking. Personal experiences, curiosity and willingness to contribute can be valuable. What matters is an applicant s interest in: Sharing their perspective. Listening to the views and experiences of others. Contributing constructively to discussions. Helping government better understand how decisions affect young people. Bringing their personal or community experiences into conversations. Engaging with climate, nature and environmental issues. This broad approach could allow the panel to hear perspectives that might otherwise be missing from national environmental discussions. The Government Wants Young People From Different Backgrounds and Experiences Diversity of experience is central to the purpose of the panel. Climate change and environmental policies do not affect every person or community in exactly the same way. A young person living in a major city, for example, may experience environmental challenges differently from someone living in a rural or agricultural community. Similarly, young people studying at university may have different perspectives from those who are working, undertaking training or following other pathways. The panel therefore aims to bring together young people with a range of experiences and perspectives. The government has emphasised the importance of reaching young people whose voices might not normally be heard in national conversations concerning climate and nature. Why Youth Perspectives Matter in UK Climate and Nature Policy The establishment of the Youth Climate and Nature Panel comes as the UK continues to pursue major climate and environmental programmes. These include efforts related to: Protecting 30% of land and sea for nature by 2030 . Supporting large-scale nature recovery. Attracting private investment into environmental improvement. Transitioning toward clean energy. Developing a net zero economy. Strengthening environmental protection. Improving climate resilience. Creating opportunities connected to green employment and industries. These programmes can have long-term consequences for today s young people. Hearing directly from younger generations may help policymakers better understand whether proposed policies are practical, fair and capable of producing lasting benefits. Building Climate and Nature Policy With Communities The Youth Climate and Nature Panel forms part of a broader approach to involving communities in policymaking. The intention is to develop policy with greater public participation rather than limiting involvement to consultation after major decisions have already been developed. Different approaches to public and youth participation are already being used across the Department for Environment, Food Rural Affairs and related organisations. For example, members of the public have contributed to the development of the government s food strategy through a Citizen Advisory Council. The Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew also operates a Youth Council that works with senior leaders, helping ensure that young people s views are reflected in organisational decision-making. The new Youth Climate and Nature Panel will provide another mechanism through which younger voices can contribute. How Many Young People Will Be Selected? A total of 15 young people will form the Youth Climate and Nature Panel. With places limited, prospective applicants should carefully review the official information and submit their applications before the deadline. Applicants should focus on communicating their genuine perspectives and experiences rather than assuming they need extensive technical knowledge. The initiative specifically values different experiences, curiosity and willingness to participate. Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026 Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the UK Government Youth Climate and Nature Panel is: Friday, 11 September 2026. Interested young people should ensure their applications are completed and submitted in accordance with the official application instructions before the deadline. Applicants are encouraged not to leave their submission until the last moment. How to Apply for the Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026 Interested applicants should visit the official GOV.UK Youth Climate and Nature Panel page to review the full application information and instructions. Because eligibility requirements, application procedures and other administrative details should always be confirmed directly from the official source, applicants should carefully read the published government guidance before submitting an application. Official application and further information: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/youth-climate-and-nature-panel Young Voices for Climate and Nature 2026 Alongside recruitment for the Youth Climate and Nature Panel, the government has launched another initiative called Young Voices for Climate and Nature . This provides children and young people aged 16 and under with an opportunity to share the climate and nature ideas that matter to them. Young people can participate through organisations and groups such as: Schools. Community groups. Sports groups. Faith groups. Other youth organisations. Importantly, contributions are not restricted to traditional written submissions. Young people can communicate their ideas in different creative formats, including: Videos. Artwork. Letters. Poems. Essays. Audio recordings. Presentations. The ideas submitted through Young Voices for Climate and Nature are expected to help inform the work of the Youth Climate and Nature Panel when it begins its work later in 2026. Young Voices for Climate and Nature Deadline The deadline for entries to Young Voices for Climate and Nature is: Friday, 23 October 2026. More information is available through the official government page: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/young-voices-for-climate-and-nature Applicants and organisations should note that this deadline is different from the Youth Climate and Nature Panel application deadline of Friday, 11 September 2026 . Schools and Youth Organisations Are Encouraged to Share the Opportunity Schools, colleges, charities, environmental networks, youth organisations and community groups can play an important role in ensuring information about the opportunity reaches eligible young people. Organisations working with young people are encouraged to share information through: Membership networks. Youth programmes. Schools and colleges. Community networks. Organisational communications channels. Environmental groups and networks. Local youth initiatives. Particular attention is encouraged toward reaching young people whose voices might not normally be represented in national climate and environmental conversations. Someone does not need an established profile as an environmental activist or expert to have a valuable perspective. Everyday experiences of communities, employment, education, farming, cities, rural life, energy, nature and environmental change can provide useful insights into how policies affect people. Why Young People Should Consider Applying Joining the Youth Climate and Nature Panel provides selected young people with an opportunity to contribute directly to conversations about issues that could shape the UK s environmental future. For a young person interested in climate change, nature, sustainability, public policy, clean energy, agriculture, green careers or the future economy, the panel could provide a significant opportunity to share ideas and experiences. It may also appeal to young people who have never previously thought of themselves as environmental advocates. The government is explicitly seeking personal perspectives alongside established environmental knowledge. For potential applicants, this means that being curious, willing to listen and prepared to share personal experiences can be relevant qualities. Key Details at a Glance Opportunity: UK Government Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026 Organisations: UK Government, with the initiative involving government work on climate and nature policy, including the Department for Environment, Food Rural Affairs and Department for Energy Security and Net Zero Number of panel members: 15 Age requirement: 16 to 25 years old Location requirement: Applicants must be based in the United Kingdom Experience required: Applicants do not need to be climate, environmental or policy experts Main purpose: To give young people opportunities to share perspectives, provide insight and advice, strengthen youth engagement and help inform government thinking on climate and nature policy Youth Climate and Nature Panel application deadline: Friday, 11 September 2026 Young Voices for Climate and Nature deadline: Friday, 23 October 2026 Official Youth Climate and Nature Panel information and application: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/youth-climate-and-nature-panel APPLY NOW Conclusion The UK Government Youth Climate and Nature Panel 2026 represents a new opportunity for young people to contribute their experiences, concerns and ideas to national conversations about climate change, nature restoration and the transition toward a more sustainable economy. Fifteen young people aged 16 to 25 will be brought together from across the UK, with members having opportunities to share their views with government, provide insight and advice, strengthen engagement with other young people and help determine the panel s priorities. Perhaps most importantly, applicants do not need to arrive with years of environmental campaigning experience or detailed knowledge of government policy. The initiative is also looking for young people whose perspectives come from their everyday lives, communities and personal experiences. Whether an applicant is interested in farming and nature recovery, renewable energy, greener cities, climate resilience, sustainable food, biodiversity, green jobs, emerging technologies or simply how environmental decisions will affect their generation, their perspective could have value. Eligible young people who want to be considered for one of the 15 positions should review the official application information and submit their application before Friday, 11 September 2026 . For younger people aged 16 and under, the separate Young Voices for Climate and Nature initiative provides another way to contribute through artwork, videos, letters, poems, essays, audio recordings, presentations and other submissions, with entries closing on Friday, 23 October 2026 . Together, these initiatives are intended to bring a wider range of younger voices into conversations about the UK s climate and natural environment and give the next generation a more meaningful role in discussions about the future they will inherit. title: Japan MIRAI AI Startup Program 2026: Applications Open for Georgian Students and Young Professionals
summary: The Government of Japan is accepting applications for the Japan’s Friendship Ties Program “MIRAI” 2026 , offering eligible university students and young professionals from Georgia an opportunity to participate in a short-term exchange program in Japan. The program available to Georgian applicants is organized under the theme “AI Startup” and is scheduled to take place in Japan from December 1 to December 7, 2026 . Applicants must be undergraduate students, graduate students or young professionals between 20 and 30 years of age. The deadline to submit the online application and all supporting documents is August 31, 2026, at 18:59 Georgia Standard Time . The MIRAI program is intended to deepen participants’ understanding of Japan, promote intellectual exchange with Japanese students and experts, strengthen international networks and create a foundation for future cooperation between Japan and participating countries. Interested candidates should study the official guidelines carefully because this is a country-specific application route. The Embassy of Japan in Georgia announcement does not represent a worldwide application call. Key Program Information Program name: Japan’s Friendship Ties Program “MIRAI” Available theme: AI Startup Organized by: Government of Japan Responsible ministry: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan Implementing platform: Japan International Cooperation Center application system Eligible applicant location: Georgia Eligible age range: 20–30 years Target applicants: Undergraduate students, graduate students and young professionals Program location: Japan Program dates for Georgian participants: December 1–7, 2026 Application deadline: August 31, 2026, at 18:59 Georgia Standard Time Deadline in UTC: August 31, 2026, at 14:59 UTC Application method: Online application with supporting documents Working language: English Official announcement: Embassy of Japan in Georgia Application guidelines: MIRAI 2026 application guidelines Application form: MIRAI 2026 online application What Is the Japan MIRAI Program? The MIRAI Program is a short-term international youth exchange initiative launched by the Government of Japan in 2015. The Japanese word “mirai” means “future.” The title is also an acronym based on the following words: Mutual understanding, Intellectual Relations and Academic exchange Initiative. The program invites promising university students, graduate students and young professionals from Europe, Central Asia and the Caucasus to participate in educational, intellectual and cultural activities connected with Japan. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan describes MIRAI as a people-to-people exchange program intended for young individuals studying or working in fields such as politics, security policy, economics, international relations, Asian studies, Japanese studies and other related disciplines. For the 2026 regional group involving Georgia, the selected theme is AI Startup. This connects the exchange with the rapidly developing fields of artificial intelligence, technology, innovation and entrepreneurship. Objectives of the MIRAI Program The MIRAI Program seeks to develop stronger long-term relationships between Japan and participating countries through direct engagement with the next generation of students, researchers, entrepreneurs and professionals. Its principal objectives include: Promoting a deeper understanding of Japan Participants are introduced to Japan’s economy, society, history, cultural diversity, politics, public institutions and diplomatic relations. Encouraging intellectual exchange The program creates opportunities for participants to exchange ideas with Japanese university students, scholars, experts and professionals. Strengthening public communication Participants are expected to communicate what they learn about Japan, its policies and its attractions through social media, presentations or other appropriate communication channels. Building international networks By bringing together participants from different countries and connecting them with Japanese institutions, the program helps establish relationships that may support future academic, professional and diplomatic cooperation. Creating a foundation for future friendship The Government of Japan intends the program to contribute to stronger relations between Japan and the participating regions over the long term. Developing future leaders MIRAI targets promising young individuals who are expected to contribute actively to their institutions, professions and wider international society. The AI Startup Theme The specific program offered to applicants from Georgia is titled AI Startup . Although the Georgian embassy announcement does not publish a complete AI-specific curriculum, the theme indicates an emphasis on the relationship between artificial intelligence, technological innovation, entrepreneurship and startup development. Applicants whose studies or professional work relate to the following areas may be particularly well positioned to explain their interest in the program: Artificial intelligence; Machine learning; Information technology; Computer science; Software development; Engineering; Data science; Digital transformation; Technology policy; Entrepreneurship; Startup development; Business innovation; Innovation management; Research commercialization; and Technology-based solutions to public or social challenges. These fields are not presented by the Embassy of Japan in Georgia as an exhaustive formal eligibility list. Undergraduate and graduate students and young professionals remain the expressly identified applicant groups. However, applicants should clearly demonstrate how their academic interests, professional experience or future ambitions connect with the AI Startup theme. Participating Countries in the AI Startup Group The wider 2026 AI Startup group covers selected countries in Central Asia and the Caucasus. According to the current announcement published by the Embassy of Japan in Kazakhstan , the participating countries are: Armenia; Azerbaijan; Georgia; Kazakhstan; Kyrgyzstan; Tajikistan; Turkmenistan; and Uzbekistan. The same official announcement states that the AI Startup group is expected to contain 12 participants in total from these eight countries . This indicates that selection is likely to be highly competitive. The Georgian embassy has not published a separate national quota, so applicants should not assume that a fixed number of positions has been reserved for Georgia. Applicants from the other participating countries should follow the application arrangements announced by the Embassy of Japan responsible for their respective country. They should not use Georgia-specific instructions unless directed to do so by the relevant Japanese diplomatic mission. Expected Program Structure The general MIRAI format includes preparatory online learning followed by an intensive program in Japan. Online Pre-Exchange Activities The official July 2026 MIRAI overview states that participants may complete online pre-exchange activities before travelling to Japan. These activities may include: Participant orientation; Guidance on sharing program experiences through social media; Lectures connected with the program theme; Virtual discussions with Japanese students; Exchanges with Japanese experts; and Practical information about the visit to Japan. A current official announcement for the same AI Startup regional group indicates that preparatory activities may include an introductory MIRAI video, a general lecture about Japan and a pre-departure lecture. Georgian participants should wait for the final schedule and instructions issued by the Embassy, JICE or program organizers. Participation in required online activities should be treated as an integral part of the program rather than an optional addition. Activities in Japan The general MIRAI model may include: Lectures on Japan and its major policies; Theme-related academic or professional sessions; Discussions with Japanese university students; Exchanges with researchers, entrepreneurs and other experts; Visits to universities and educational institutions; Visits to Japanese companies or research organizations; Exposure to advanced and traditional industries; Visits to cultural, historical or technological sites; Travel to a city or region outside Tokyo; Meetings or exchanges with local communities; Workshops and group discussions; A reporting or debriefing session; and Preparation of ideas or plans for activities after returning home. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ sample itinerary refers to approximately four days in Tokyo and two days in another Japanese city. It also identifies the possibility of a homestay and visits to Japanese companies, research institutes and historical locations. However, this is a general sample itinerary. The exact institutions, cities, companies, speakers and activities for the 2026 AI Startup group have not been specified in the Georgian announcement and may change. Who Can Apply? The Embassy of Japan in Georgia expressly identifies the following applicant groups: Undergraduate students; Graduate students; and Young professionals. Applicants must be between 20 and 30 years old . Because this is a Georgia-specific application announcement, candidates should be connected with Georgia and satisfy the nationality, institutional or residence requirements contained in the detailed application guidelines. The shared 2026 MIRAI requirements, as summarized on other official Japanese embassy pages for the same application cycle, also indicate that applicants should generally: Have sufficient English proficiency to participate actively in lectures and discussions; Have a good academic or professional background; Be in suitable physical and mental health; Be capable of participating in a busy schedule that may involve extensive walking; Understand and support the objectives of the MIRAI Program; Be willing to communicate their experiences during and after the program; Not have lived in Japan continuously for more than six months; Not have previously participated in MIRAI or a similar exchange funded by the Government of Japan; and Be available for all compulsory online and in-person activities. Candidates must consult the current application guidelines for the definitive wording of every condition. English-Language Requirement MIRAI activities are generally conducted in English. Participants may need to: Follow lectures and presentations; Participate in technical and policy discussions; Communicate with Japanese students and experts; Take part in group workshops; Explain their academic or professional background; Present ideas during reporting sessions; and interact with participants from other countries. Applicants should therefore possess practical spoken and written English proficiency. A formal English-language test score is not mentioned in the Embassy of Japan in Georgia announcement, but candidates should be able to participate confidently in an international English-speaking environment. Potential Benefits of Participating The program may provide selected participants with valuable academic, professional and cross-cultural exposure. Direct Experience of Japan Participants can develop a first-hand understanding of Japanese society, culture, institutions, industries and public policies. Exposure to AI and Startup Innovation The AI Startup theme may provide opportunities to explore how Japan approaches artificial intelligence, research, commercialization, entrepreneurship and technology-based innovation. Interaction With Japanese Experts Participants may engage with academics, researchers, entrepreneurs, students and representatives of relevant institutions. International Networking The regional group is expected to bring together participants from eight countries, allowing participants to build relationships beyond their home institutions and national boundaries. Academic and Professional Development Lectures, workshops, institutional visits and group activities can strengthen participants’ analytical, communication, intercultural and leadership abilities. Cultural Learning The program combines thematic learning with exposure to Japanese history, cultural practices, local communities and regional industries. Future Cooperation Connections established through the program may support future research, educational partnerships, startup cooperation or other professional engagement with Japan and participating countries. Financial Coverage and Personal Expenses The Embassy of Japan in Georgia’s announcement does not provide a detailed list of covered expenses. It therefore does not, by itself, justify describing the opportunity as fully funded. Applicants must read the 2026 application guidelines and Letter of Understanding to confirm: Whether international airfare is covered; Which meals and transportation costs are included; Whether accommodation is arranged; The scope of travel insurance; Visa-related arrangements; Costs that remain the participant’s responsibility; Medical and vaccination exclusions; Cancellation charges; and Whether any cash allowance is available. Previous official MIRAI guidelines have commonly provided arranged economy-class airfare, accommodation and specified program-related expenses while leaving participants responsible for certain personal costs. However, previous-year arrangements should not be treated as a binding promise for the 2026 AI Startup group. Applicants should obtain confirmation from the current guidelines or organizers before making any financial assumptions. Required Application Documents Applicants must submit five categories of supporting documents through the online application system. 1. Valid Passport Copy Applicants must upload a copy of the passport’s photograph and personal-information page. The passport copy may be in color or black and white, but it must be: Clear; Complete; Properly enlarged; and Legible in every part. All personal and passport information must be visible. If the applicant does not have a passport that will remain valid during the program, the applicant must renew or extend it promptly. A copy of the renewed or extended passport must be submitted no later than one month before the program begins. Applicants should not upload a cropped, blurred, dark or incomplete passport image. 2. Letter of Understanding Applicants must carefully read the conditions contained in the Letter of Understanding before applying. The applicant must: Agree to the stated conditions; Sign the document; and Upload every page of the document. Uploading only the signed page is insufficient. All pages must be included. 3. Personal Information and GDPR Privacy Policy Applicants must read the document titled “Handling of Personal Information and the General Data Protection Regulation Privacy Policy.” The document must be signed and uploaded with the application. Applicants should understand how their personal data may be collected, processed, shared and used for program administration and reporting. 4. Academic Transcript or Proof of Enrollment or Employment The required evidence depends on the applicant’s current status. For Students Students must submit an academic transcript clearly displaying the name of their educational institution. First-year students who do not yet have a transcript from their current institution must submit: The most recent academic transcript from their high school or previous university; and A current Certificate of Enrollment issued by their university or graduate school. Both documents are required in this situation. For Young Professionals Young professionals must submit a Certificate of Employment. The certificate must clearly identify the applicant’s current employer. 5. Recent Headshot Applicants must upload a recent personal photograph taken within the previous three months. The photograph may be in color or black and white. The photograph should clearly show the applicant’s face and should be suitable for identification and program administration. Step-by-Step Application Process Step 1: Review the Official Announcement Read the Embassy of Japan in Georgia announcement and confirm that you fall within the specified applicant group and age range. Step 2: Read the Complete Guidelines Study the official MIRAI 2026 application guidelines carefully. Pay particular attention to: Nationality and institutional requirements; Age calculations; English proficiency; Previous residence in Japan; Previous participation in Japanese government programs; Health requirements; Program attendance obligations; Financial arrangements; Cancellation conditions; Personal-data processing; and Post-program responsibilities. Step 3: Prepare the Required Documents Obtain the passport copy, signed forms, transcript or employment certificate and recent headshot. Make sure that every document is complete and readable. Step 4: Complete the Online Application in English Access the MIRAI 2026 application form and enter accurate personal, academic and professional information. Applicants should not make claims that cannot be supported by their submitted documents. Step 5: Upload All Supporting Documents Check that all five required categories have been uploaded in the correct format. Pay particular attention to the requirement to upload every page of the Letter of Understanding. Step 6: Review the Application Before submission, verify: Name spelling; Date of birth; Passport details; Contact information; Educational or employment information; Uploaded file clarity; Signatures; Document completeness; and Consistency between the form and supporting documents. Step 7: Submit Before the Deadline Submit the complete application no later than: August 31, 2026, at 18:59 Georgia Standard Time. Applicants should submit early enough to address internet, file-upload or application-platform problems. How to Strengthen an Application Although the Embassy has not published a detailed selection rubric, a competitive applicant should clearly show: A genuine interest in the AI Startup theme; Relevant academic, technical, entrepreneurial or professional experience; Strong motivation to learn from Japan; The ability to contribute meaningfully to discussions; A clear connection between the program and future goals; Sufficient English communication skills; Evidence of academic or professional performance; An interest in international cooperation; Willingness to share learning after the program; The ability to complete all required activities; and Potential to use the experience for wider institutional or community benefit. Applicants should avoid relying only on a general desire to visit Japan. The application should explain why the AI Startup theme matters to their studies, work or future contribution. Important Responsibilities of Selected Participants MIRAI is structured as an active exchange, not simply a sightseeing visit. Selected participants should be prepared to: Attend compulsory online preparatory sessions; Follow the complete official itinerary; Participate in lectures and workshops; Engage in discussions with Japanese students and experts; Cooperate with participants from other countries; Follow instructions issued by the organizers; Respect Japanese laws, institutional rules and cultural expectations; Share their experiences appropriately through social media or other communication channels; Participate in reporting or debriefing activities; and Complete any required post-program questionnaires or follow-up activities. Applicants should confirm their availability for the entire program before applying. Selection and Notification The Embassy of Japan in Georgia has not published: The number of places specifically allocated to Georgia; A national interview date; A detailed scoring system; A date for announcing shortlisted candidates; or A final selection-notification date. The wider AI Startup group is expected to include only 12 participants from eight countries, so completing an application does not guarantee selection. Applicants should monitor their email carefully after applying, including spam or junk folders, because any request for clarification, interview invitation or selection result may be communicated electronically. Common Application Mistakes to Avoid Applicants should avoid: Applying without reading the complete guidelines; Assuming that the program is open worldwide; Submitting after the Georgia-specific deadline; Uploading an unreadable passport copy; Uploading only the signature page of the Letter of Understanding; Forgetting to sign the privacy document; Submitting a transcript without the institution’s name; Failing to include a Certificate of Enrollment when required; Submitting an employment certificate without the employer’s name; Using an outdated photograph; Providing inconsistent information across documents; Misrepresenting previous residence or program participation in Japan; Assuming that all expenses are covered without verifying the current terms; or Treating the program as tourism rather than an educational and professional exchange. Application Deadline The final deadline for applicants using the Embassy of Japan in Georgia route is: August 31, 2026, at 18:59 Georgia Standard Time. This corresponds to 14:59 UTC and 23:59 Japan Standard Time on August 31, 2026. Applicants should follow the time stated by the Embassy of Japan in Georgia, even if MIRAI announcements issued in other countries show different local times.
